guitar.evidence: Johnny Winter is famously associated with the Gibson Firebird (especially the non-reverse Firebird) for much of his career, well documented in blues-rock guitar history.

tone.target: nasal blues fuzz with raw boogie bite
tone.profile: nasal blues fuzz with raw boogie bite
tone.summary: A raw, high-gain signal chain utilizing Fuzz for the core tone, followed by a British amp model (UK 45) and a punchy cabinet to deliver nasal, boogie bite.

rig.name: Johnny Winter - Mojo Boogie - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain fuzz noise and maintain clarity.
Provide initial grit and boost the attack before the fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here to simulate a slight dirty edge/boost, complementing the main fuzz tone without sounding like generic overdrive.

alternatives.reason: A simple boost could also provide necessary attack.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the core 'nasal blues fuzz' and aggressive attack required for boogie tones.

alternatives.reason: A general Fuzz model could also work, but Red Haze is better suited for the specific blues/nasal tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall-ish crunch and punchy British tone.

alternatives.reason: A slightly different flavor of UK amp, but the UK 45 is more associated with classic blues rock.

blocks.purpose: Provide the necessary punch and mid-range focus associated with small to mid cabs.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for a slightly different cabinet voicing.
